transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-15 16:30 PST | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Daniel Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood Solutions), Rajiv Menon (CTO - Lumos), Ella Stone (Head of IT), Tomas Alvarez (Lead ML Eng), Meera Shah (Compliance)

Summary (auto): Initial feasibility discovery for fully air-gapped on-prem Redwood Private deployment. Topics: offline update mechanism, hardware constraints (GPU availability), KMS/HSM integration, audit/logging, timeline for pilot.

[00:00] Daniel Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros from our side, I'm Daniel, AE on the account, Priya is our SE, Maya covers solutions for regulated deployments. how about you all?
[00:14] Rajiv Menon: Rajiv here. We're trying to understand if Redwood can run inside our air-locked datacenter. high level: regulatory constraints, no egress, manual media updates only, and a pretty strict change window schedule.
[00:29] Ella Stone: yep. and we have limited GPU options — procurement cycle is slow; likely we'll start with 2x A10 or maybe 4x T4 depending on availability. can't promise A100s right away.
[00:41] Priya Rao: okay that helps. quick clarifying q: when you say "manual media", do you mean physically shipping USBs/secure drives into the site, or a locked jump box with controlled sync?
[00:51] Ella Stone: physical transfer, vetted and scanned, signed manifest. we do have a secure staging machine that can accept signed artifacts — no direct internet.
[01:02] Daniel Kim: got it. we have a few customers running in that mode. there are a couple of patterns — fully air-gapped where updates are via signed tarball on physical media, and a semi-isolated pattern where a bastion host pulls from a repo in a locked network. both viable depending on policy.
[01:20] Tomas Alvarez: what's the size of the runtime? and model bundles — are they enormous? our models are 13B and 70B variants; curious about footprint and whether we can run quantized versions.
[01:31] Priya Rao: runtime itself is modest — the server and orchestration bits are small relative to model weights. for weights: yes, you can use lower-bit quantized artifacts (8-bit/4-bit) we ship model binaries as tarballs with checksums and signature. our private package supports on-disk KV cache; you'll want at least X TB of storage for larger models — we'll send a sizing sheet.
[01:52] Rajiv Menon: X TB? we need numbers. our storage inside the airlock is LUN-based, limited. also curious about GPU memory — if we only have A10s with 24GB, can we still host 13B efficiently?
[02:06] Priya Rao: 13B is usually fine on 24GB with 4-bit quant; 70B will be tricky — requires model sharding across GPUs or bigger memory. We can run a CPU fallback too but cost/latency tradeoffs.
[02:19] Ella Stone: tradeoffs will matter. medical inference latency target is sub-450ms p95 for snippet-level clinical summarization. is that feasible on A10s?
[02:29] Priya Rao: depends on batching. for single-shot low-latency, 24GB GPUs might hit 300-600ms for 13B with optimized kernels, but 70B likely exceeds your SLO unless you do model distillation or dedicated high-memory cards.
[02:45] Meera Shah: security-wise we need KMS integration with our HSM (Thales/Cavium) and key ceremony requirements. are we able to bring our own KMS?
[02:56] Daniel Kim: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. we ship an integration point; keys never leave your possession. for air-gapped installs there's a local KMS connector that runs inside the cluster and interfaces with HSM over network fabric. we'll share the HSM connector spec.
[03:12] Priya Rao: also audit logs — we can emit detailed request/response metadata to your SIEM downstream; for fully air-gapped setups logs can be stored on a secure endpoint, and exported via signed bundles for compliance review.
[03:26] Tomas Alvarez: what's the update cadence? our compliance team wants quarterly security patches and model updates only after validation. can we control rollout windows?
[03:35] Daniel Kim: yes, rollouts are configurable. for Private we support canary, manual approval gates, and completely manual offline updates. standard flow for air-gap: we produce a signed package, you pull it in, run a local validation job (we can provide a containerized validation harness), then flip traffic when ready.
[03:56] Rajiv Menon: how about offline telemetry? we cannot permit telemetry leaving the network. we still want traces for debugging — any approach?
[04:05] Priya Rao: telemetry can be disabled. we provide a local tracing UI that writes traces to local storage and artifacts can be exported as zipped traces for Red teams. zero egress required.
[04:15] Ella Stone: excellent. procurement question: do you do hardware procurement or we provide BOM?
[04:21] Daniel Kim: typically customers provide hardware. we produce a recommended BOM and verified configurations — we also have preferred partners for procurement if you want an end-to-end delivery (this is a separate channel).
[04:33] Tomas Alvarez: can we bring our own model weights? we train in-house, and must not share models externally.
[04:39] Priya Rao: absolutely. Redwood Private supports BYOW (bring your own weights). bundle them into our expected tarball format and install locally. we provide a validation tool to ensure runtime compatibility.
[04:50] Rajiv Menon: any pre-approved SOC/ISO attestations for the platform or do we need an on-site audit?
[04:58] Daniel Kim: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001 for our control plane; for Private installs we provide our compliance package and can support evidence collection for your auditors. on-site audit of customer environment is typically done by your team with our engineers present if requested.
[05:12] Meera Shah: what about RBAC and SSO? we have OKTA — must map to groups and limit deploy permissions to a small ops group.
[05:20] Priya Rao: we support SAML/Okta, SCIM provisioning, fine-grained RBAC. we can pre-map roles and integrate with your AD/LDAP.
[05:29] Ella Stone: networking details: we have isolated VLANs, no outbound NAT. how do we bootstrap images and updates?
[05:36] Priya Rao: two patterns: 1) physically transport signed artifacts and run our offline installer; 2) use a dedicated air-gapped bastion that you control which pulls from an internal staging repo (still no public internet). both are supported. installer supports explicit manifests and digest checking.
[05:51] Rajiv Menon: what about CVE patching for the runtime? we have strict windows for rolling patches.
[05:58] Daniel Kim: we publish patch advisories and a CVE matrix. for Private, you control when patches are applied; we can provide a backported urgent patch as a signed package for out-of-band installs if critical.
[06:12] Tomas Alvarez: curious about orchestration — do you require Kubernetes inside the airlock?
[06:18] Priya Rao: we support Kubernetes (tested with K8s 1.25+), but also offer a lightweight runtime mode for environments that won't run full K8s. The lightweight runtime is container-native and managed via systemd units; both modes support similar features but K8s gives you easier scaling and pod-level controls.
[06:36] Ella Stone: client-side encryption for persisted KV cache? we prefer at-rest encryption with tenant keys.
[06:42] Priya Rao: yes — at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys is supported for model cache and logs.
[06:48] Daniel Kim: quick note on performance: with model quantization and our optimized kernels, we've seen token throughput improvements of 2.5x on 4-bit compared to 8-bit. we'll include benchmark artifacts specific to 13B/quantized runs for A10 and T4.
[07:05] Tomas Alvarez: can we run offline evals? like push prompts and compare outputs across model versions locally?
[07:10] Priya Rao: yes, we provide a local eval harness — you can point it to your prompt corpus and run regression checks before promoting a model. results stay on-prem.
[07:20] Rajiv Menon: timeline — if we buy Dedicated licenses for private, how long to pilot?
[07:25] Daniel Kim: typical pilot for air-gapped is 6-8 weeks from contract signature: hardware procurement + install (2–3 weeks depending on procurement), then install and baseline (1 week), validation and pilot (2–3 weeks). we'll try to accelerate if hardware is in-hand.
[07:40] Meera Shah: can we do a small sandbox in our staging network (semi-isolated) before fully offline?
[07:45] Daniel Kim: absolutely recommended. start in staging with a bastion repo pattern, then move to fully air-gapped when process is ironed out.
[07:56] Ella Stone: pricing — do you price per-seat or per-GPU?
[08:00] Daniel Kim: Private is typically subscription plus a per-GPU/throughput licensing component; Dedicated is committed capacity. we'll send a ballpark pricing sheet based on your expected token volumes.
[08:12] Tomas Alvarez (mumbling): also need to know if Redwood will sign off on our change control docs...
[08:16] Daniel Kim: we can review your change control process and annotate where our operations need to fit.
[08:22] Priya Rao: quick technical aside — if you only have 2x A10s, we recommend starting with 13B quantized and keeping the 70B as a follow-on with larger cards or inference-only sharded instances.
[08:36] Ella Stone: sounds reasonable. any gotchas we should know?
[08:40] Priya Rao: two things: 1) ensure NIC bandwidth between GPUs for sharded models; 2) plan for storage IOPS if you use large model cache and many concurrent requests. we'll share recommended NIC and storage specs.
[08:55] Rajiv Menon: excellent. next steps recap?
[09:00] Daniel Kim: I'll send the air-gapped runbook, the SOC/ISO attestation, and a preliminary hardware checklist. Priya will draft the workshop agenda and hardware sizing. we'll propose Feb 2-3 for the technical workshop.
[09:15] Meera Shah: please include compliance artifacts and the HSM connector spec in the email.
[09:20] Daniel Kim: will do. thanks everyone.

End of meeting.

Notes: occasional mis-transcription of product names observed (e.g., "airlock" vs "air-locked"), speaker overlap at 08:12. References shared: Redwood air-gap runbook (link sent after call), hardware checklist (attachment forthcoming), SOC2 attestation (PDF).
